name: Agiloft
description: Agiloft is a configurable contract lifecycle management platform whose customer knowledgebases define their own tables, fields, permissions, workflows, and API schemas.
agentUseSummary: Agiloft cannot yet be connected as a generic Relay agent provider. Although Agiloft supports REST, SOAP, JWT, and OAuth 2.0, every customer knowledgebase has a generated schema and permission model. Relay has no universal privacy-safe record or metadata contract to publish without first binding a reviewed customer schema, table allowlist, field projection, dedicated API identity, and exact environment.

blocked.label: Connect an unreviewed Agiloft knowledgebase
blocked.description: Relay will not request a customer login, password, JWT, OAuth token, or client secret without an exact instance, knowledgebase, dedicated identity, and reviewed authorization design.

blocked.label: Access dynamic knowledgebase records
blocked.description: Customer-defined tables, fields, records, attachments, contracts, people, comments, workflows, permissions, and generated schemas are blocked until explicitly allowlisted and projected.

blocked.label: Mutate or administer Agiloft
blocked.description: Record creation, update, deletion, workflow actions, attachment access, table or field changes, user or group administration, and web-service configuration are blocked.

blocked.label: Use legacy, inferred, or arbitrary API calls
blocked.description: Relay will not place passwords in URLs, accept arbitrary instance paths or table names, scrape generated Swagger, automate the website, reuse sessions, or infer private operations.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay has a customer-schema-bound, least-privilege Agiloft integration contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No universal schema-safe Agiloft operation is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No universal schema-safe Agiloft operation is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Agiloft exposes powerful customer-knowledgebase-specific APIs whose generated tables, fields, Swagger documentation, and effective permissions differ by deployment. The generic candidate lacks a reviewed instance, knowledgebase schema, table and field allowlist, dedicated least-privilege API identity, exact origin, and stable privacy projection, so publishing a generic connection would either fabricate semantics or expose arbitrary customer records.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request credentials or expose Connect. Reconsider Agiloft only after defining a distributable schema-binding flow that validates an exact HTTPS instance and knowledgebase, imports and reviews the generated schema, requires a dedicated REST-enabled identity, allowlists specific tables and fields, strictly projects responses, and proves disconnect and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Agiloft documents Authorization Code and PKCE support, knowledgebase-local OAuth2 Client Setup, per-knowledgebase REST documentation, and API operations that depend on custom identifiers and table fields.

Agiloft documents broad search/read/create/update/delete and workflow authority, generated WSDL schemas tied to knowledgebase data structures and fields, required API enablement, and access governed by the API user's groups and permissions.

Agiloft documents knowledgebase-specific REST groups, IP allowlists and denylists, CORS configuration, and web-service security controls, confirming that deployment-specific authorization is required.

Agiloft's record-read operation requires customer knowledgebase, table, user authority, and record identity and can return arbitrary customer-defined fields, including people and organization data; no universal privacy-safe projection is defined.
